claims.claim_text: Bitdeer operates 10 datacenters with aggregate electrical capacity of 1,744.0 MW as of March 31, 2026, scaled from 795 MW in March 2023; total pipeline capacity 1,259.5 MW (US, Canada, Malaysia), bringing total potential global capacity to 3,003.5 MW.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: 1744.0 MW operating; 1259.5 MW pipeline; 3003.5 MW total
claims.source_quote: we currently operate ten datacenters across multiple countries including the United States, Norway, Bhutan, Ethiopia and Malaysia, with an aggregate electrical capacity of 1,744.0 MW as of March 31, 2026... We expect to achieve access to a total electrical capacity of approximately 3,003.5 MW thereafter.

claims.claim_text: Massillon, Ohio datacenter is operational with 121 MW of capacity (with 26 MW fire-damaged in November 2025 being rebuilt, plus 74 MW additional phases in Q2 2026); represents a flagship US AI/colocation conversion site.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: Massillon Ohio 121 MW operational + 74/26 MW pipeline
claims.source_quote: Our datacenter in Massillon, Ohio became operational in 2025 and had 121 MW electrical capacity in use as of March 31, 2026... An additional approximately 74 MW is expected to be energized in phases during the second quarter of 2026.

claims.claim_text: Clarington, Ohio pipeline site has 570 MW under contract with a local utility, intended for colocation use; construction timing affected by active litigation by American Heavy Plate Solutions (AHP) over leasehold/restrictive-covenant claims.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: Clarington OH 570 MW under utility contract (colocation; litigation risk)
claims.source_quote: Clarington Datacenter. We have 570 MW of power under contract with a local utility. The timing of power availability and construction may be affected by ongoing legal proceedings filed by American Heavy Plate Solutions, LLC.

claims.claim_text: Niles, Ohio: BTDR owns 41.8 acres at a 300 MW grid-interconnected development site intended for colocation/AI cloud use, energization slated Q4 2028, with executed transmission-line extension agreement with local utility.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: Niles OH 300 MW grid-interconnected; Q4 2028; colocation/AI cloud
claims.source_quote: Niles Datacenter. We own 41.8 acres of land at a 300 MW grid-interconnected development site intended for colocation or AI cloud use, and have entered into a transmission line extension agreement with a local utility company.

claims.claim_text: Bitdeer offers AI cloud services in Asia powered by NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD H100, H200, B200 systems and recently deployed NVIDIA GB200 NVL72; AI cloud services generated US$6.769M revenue in FY2025 (1.1% of total $620.3M revenue) — vs $3.45M FY2024 and $1k FY2023.

claims.source_quote: we operate one of the first cloud service platforms in Asia that offers AI cloud services powered by NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD H100, H200, B200 systems and the recently deployed NVIDIA GB200 NVL72... AI cloud services 6,769 1.1 3,450 1.0 1 0.0

claims.claim_text: In March 2026 BTDR's Norway subsidiary Tydal Data Center AS executed a design-and-construction (EPC) contract with Data Center Installations AS to convert the existing 225 MW mining datacenter in Tydal, Norway into an AI datacenter (Tydal Phase 2: 175 MW Q4 2026 listed as 'crypto converting to colocation').
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: Tydal Norway AI conversion EPC signed March 27, 2026 with DCI; 225 MW site
claims.source_quote: In March 2026, Tydal Data Center AS, our subsidiary, entered into a contract for design and construction (the 'Tydal EPC Agreement') with Data Center Installations AS... for the conversion and upgrading of our existing datacenter in Tydal, Norway into an AI datacenter.

claims.claim_text: Customer concentration FY2025: Customer B 16.65%, Customer C 15.81%, Customer D 12.20%, Customer E 10.28% of revenue (i.e. four customers each >10%, aggregate ~55% of $620M). Customer A (related party — BIT Group — hosting) was 19.05% in FY2023 but <10% in FY2024/FY2025. No customers are named in the 20-F.

claims.claim_text: Heavy related-party financial dependence on BIT Group (controlled by chairman Jihan Wu): US$521.8M of borrowings outstanding as of Dec 31, 2025 (vs $0 in 2024), plus $135.6M cryptocurrency receivable from related party; multiple facility expansions through April 2026 ($516.4M aggregate outstanding under BIT Assets Collateralized Loan; new 6,000 BTC facility entered Feb–Mar 2026). Custody of substantially all crypto is with BIT Group.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: BIT Group related-party borrowings $521.8M; $135.6M crypto receivable; new 6,000 BTC facility Feb–Mar 2026
claims.source_quote: the loans from BIT Group, a related party, of US$521.8 million... On April 15, 2025, the Group entered into a loan agreement (the 'BIT Assets Collateralized Loan') with BIT Group for a financing facility of up to US$200.0 million [later raised to $400M; further $150M; plus BIT BTC Collateralized Loan $400M; plus Feb 2026 6,000 BTC facility]... substantially all of the Group's cryptocurrencies were held in custody by BIT Group.

claims.claim_text: Liquidity / dilution stress: cash dropped from $476.3M (Dec 2024) to $149.4M (Dec 2025); negative operating cash flow of $1,738.7M in FY2025 (vs $622M in FY2024); financing via $751M convertible notes net proceeds, $668M related-party borrowings, $351M ordinary share issuance in 2025, with additional $375M Feb 2026 5.00% convertible senior notes due 2032.
claims.subject: BTDR
claims.object_value: cash $149M; FY2025 op cash flow ($1.74B); +$751M converts + $668M RPT loans + $351M equity + Feb 2026 $375M converts
